title: Senior's toolkit: everyday commits
summary: The status, diff, staging and log commands experienced people type every day, with the flags that matter.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: everyday commits
steps.body: These are the commands behind every clean commit: look before you stage, stage only what you mean, check again, then commit.

toolkit.what: A short status: one line per file plus the branch and how far it is ahead of or behind its upstream.
flags: short format: `M` modified, `A` added, `??` untracked; left column staged, right column not
toolkit.when: before every add and every commit

toolkit.what: Shows exactly what the next commit will contain. Plain `git diff` shows only what is not staged yet.
flags: changed words inline, good for prose and config

toolkit.what: Stage hunk by hunk, so a debug line or an unrelated fix stays out of the commit.
flags: patch mode: `y` stage, `n` skip, `s` split the hunk, `e` edit it, `q` quit
record a new file as intent-to-add so `-p` can see it
toolkit.when: whenever one file holds more than one change

toolkit.what: Unstage a file and keep your edits. Without `--staged` it throws the working-tree edits away.
flags: reset the index entry to HEAD, leave the file alone
pick hunks to unstage or discard
take the content from another commit

toolkit.what: Opens the editor with the full diff under the message, so you write the message while reading the change.
flags: show the staged diff in the editor (not saved in the message)
add staged changes to the last commit, keep its message (only before you push)
toolkit.when: every commit; `--amend` for the typo you just noticed

toolkit.what: The history at a glance: every branch, where they fork and where they join.
flags: every ref, not just the current branch
the full patches that touched one path
toolkit.when: before you merge, rebase or push

toolkit.what: Prints a file as it was in any commit, without checking anything out.
flags: what a commit changed, as a file list

toolkit.what: Says which .gitignore file and line ignores a path. Ends the guessing when a file will not show up.
flags: print the source file, line number and pattern
check the pattern even if the file is already tracked

steps.prompt: Match each command to what it does.
pairs: stage some hunks of a file, not all of it
show what the next commit will contain
fold staged changes into the last commit

steps.prompt: Show every branch as a compact drawing of the history.
steps.explain: `--oneline` gives one short line per commit, `--graph` draws the lines, `--all` includes every branch and tag, not only HEAD. The three can go in any order on the command line.

steps.prompt: You ran `git add .` and `git status -sb` now shows `A  .env` next to your real change. The file holds local passwords. You have not committed. What do you run?
options: `git commit` and remove it in the next commit
steps.explain: `restore --staged` takes it out of the index and leaves the file on disk. `reset --hard` throws away your real change too, `git rm` deletes the file, and committing puts the passwords into history, where they stay even after a later delete.

steps.prompt: You created `build/notes.md` but `git status` never lists it, and nobody remembers ignoring it. What is the fastest way to find out why?
options: Read every `.gitignore` file in the repository
steps.explain: `check-ignore -v` prints the exact file, line and pattern (for example `.gitignore:12:build/`). `status --ignored` only shows that it is ignored, not why, and `add -f` forces it in without fixing the rule.

steps.prompt: Which commands only look, and which change the index or history?
Put a careful commit in order: check, stage the right hunks, check what is staged, commit with the diff in view.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Run `git status -sb` and `git diff --staged` before every commit, and `git add -p` whenever a file holds two changes. Reviewers notice small, clean commits, and you never have to explain a stray debug line or a committed `.env`.
